text.en: Two small glands, the thyroid and the pancreas, control your metabolism and blood sugar.

The aim is to identify the thyroid gland and the pancreas (islets of Langerhans) from a model or chart and write their location, hormones and functions.
The thyroid is a bilobed gland in the neck on either side of the trachea. It secretes triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4), which raise the metabolic rate and regulate growth. Lack of thyroxine causes goitre, myxoedema and cretinism, and excess causes Graves' disease.
The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin from beta cells and glucagon from alpha cells. Insulin converts glucose to glycogen; glucagon converts glycogen to glucose, and they keep the blood sugar at 80 to 120 mg/dl. Less insulin causes diabetes mellitus.
